A project roster has been derived from the canonical roster. Your job is to FALSIFY it, not to admire it.

The codelines it claims to be specialised for:
__CODELINE_CONTEXT__

THE ENTRIES UNDER REVIEW ARE BELOW, canonical text and derived text side by side. You are given
them directly because a roster is far too large to read through tools in one pass — that is what
made an earlier review answer that there was nothing to review. Judge what is here. This is a
BATCH: other entries are judged in their own passes, so never report that agents are missing.

__PAIR_BLOCK__

Use your tools for one thing only: checking whether a claim a derived persona makes about a
codeline is actually true. You have the source and the code; a judgement you could have made without opening either is not a review.

## What makes a roster defective

A RULE WAS WEAKENED. The derived persona may change what an agent KNOWS. It may not change what an agent is REQUIRED TO DO. If the canonical persona forbids something, demands evidence for a finding, or names a check that must pass, and the derived one softens or drops it, that is a blocking defect. Compare the two texts; do not rely on the derived one reading sensibly on its own.

A CLAIM ABOUT THE CODELINE IS FALSE. A persona asserting a framework, a directory, a helper or a command that is not there is worse than a generic sentence, because the agent will act on it and the next reader cannot tell which claims were verified. Check the ones you can; report the ones you checked.

AN ANCESTOR IS NOT CLOSE. Every entry names a canonical ancestor and inherits its ladder, its tool grant and its output contract from it. An entry whose work is nothing like its ancestor's has inherited a budget and a set of tools that do not fit the job.

AN AGENT LOST ITS PURPOSE. Specialisation replaces what an agent knows, never what it is for. A derived persona that has become a different agent means the pipeline will invoke it for the original work.

## What is NOT a defect

Content that differs from canonical. That is the point of the exercise, and difference alone is never a finding.

A persona that is shorter, plainer, or omits a generic aside that does not apply to this codeline.

An agent you judge irrelevant to this project. You cannot know which seams a run will reach, and the roster must cover every canonical agent.

## Evidence

Every finding names the agent, states which of the four defects it is, and quotes what you read — the canonical line and the derived line, or the path you opened and what was there. A finding without that is discarded before anyone sees it, so an unsupported one costs you the finding.

Return no findings if you find none. An empty finding list from a review that RAN is the correct answer for a sound roster.

THE VERDICT AND THE FINDINGS MUST AGREE. If you answer 'defects_found' you must list what you found — a verdict condemning the roster while naming nothing cannot be acted on or argued with, and it is discarded as a review that did not substantiate itself. If nothing you checked failed, the honest answer is 'sound' with no findings; that is a real result, not a weaker one.

## Project-specific guidance for this review

**Codeline**: gotransit (Next.js + React + TypeScript) at /home/bradleyjerome/projects/metrolinx/next.gotransit.com

**Commands to verify**:
- Tests: `npm test` (runs jest; component spec file exists at src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/CheckoutForm.spec.tsx)
- Type-check: TypeScript compilation (tsconfig.json present)
- Pre-commit enforcement: husky runs lint-staged and validates branch names against ^(feature|bugfix|tech|release|hotfix)/[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+(/[a-z0-9-]+)?$
- Commit message validation: commitlint with jira plugin enforces conventional commit format

**Stack conventions to verify claims against**:
- Next.js page structure (pages/ directory for routes)
- React hooks and react-hook-form patterns (heavily used; verify imports exist if named)
- TypeScript strict mode (verify types if assertions are made)
- TailwindCSS for styling (verify class names and tailwind.config.js if claimed)
- Directory structure: src/components/, src/pages/, __tests__/ convention for test files
- Next-auth for authentication (declared dependency; verify integration claims)

**Traps in this stack**: Branch name validation is strict and pre-commit enforcement is active—a derived persona claiming lenient naming or skipped hooks without evidence is suspicious. Husky integration means any claim about commit message format must align with .husky configuration and commitlint rules. Next.js API routes and middleware have specific patterns; verify path and export shapes if named.
